generation.final_prompt:
Rendering style:
Create an authored editorial illustration for a serious technology newspaper.

Direction:
- authored editorial print language
- deliberate simplified shapes with clear focal hierarchy
- restrained limited palette
- subtle physical print texture
- controlled abstraction and strong negative space
- non-photorealistic but factually grounded representation
- newspaper and social-card readability

Fixed factual and safety restrictions:
- Do not render visible text, captions, headlines, or newspaper typography.
- Do not render logos or trademarks.
- Do not fabricate visible factual evidence.
- Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
- Do not imitate a named or living artist.

Profile-specific exclusions:
- glossy CGI
- luxury product render
- generic futuristic concept art
- cyberpunk or neon
- glowing circuit-board decoration
- floating particles
- heroic centered hardware
- server rack treated as monument or skyscraper
- generic server room
- advertising composition
- airbrushed gradients
- synthetic chrome
- excessive pseudo-technical detail
- malformed or visible text
- labels
- diagrams with words

Exact source facts:
Title: OPENAI IS OPEN TO SLOWING CUTTING-EDGE AI, CEO SAM ALTMAN TELLS STAFF
Summary: OpenAI is considering slowing down development of cutting-edge AI. The company has raised concerns about its advanced AI systems, saying that model development should be paused due to safety concerns. The company's researchers have gone viral for making comments saying OpenAI's technology will kill humanity by the end of the decade.
Title: ANTHROPIC ALIGNMENT LEAD SAYS AI HAS >10% CHANCE OF KILLING HUMANITY
Summary: Anthropic Alignment Science Lead Evan Hubinger said he personally believes there is a greater than 10% chance AI could “kill all humans” within the next decade. He added that Anthropic still does not have a clear solution for aligning superintelligent AI, following another researcher's resignation over the pace of development.
Title: OPENAI BOARD MEMBER WARNS INDUSTRY ISN'T READY FOR LOSS-OF-CONTROL RISKS
Summary: OpenAI nonprofit board member Paul Christiano says the industry is not currently on track to prevent a potentially catastrophic loss of control over advanced AI. His warning adds to growing concern around how quickly increasingly autonomous systems are being developed.

Editorial idea:
The AI industry is confronting a widening gap between accelerating capability and unresolved control risks, with leaders publicly considering whether development should slow.

Central subject:
Advanced AI development facing internal warnings about catastrophic loss of control.

Visual relationship:
A fast-moving process is being interrupted by its own safety checks: the same institutions advancing frontier systems are questioning whether they can control the outcome.

Composition:
Show a long industrial production line carrying sealed, indistinct stages of development toward a bright opening, while several workers at different points pull emergency stop cords and examine warning gauges. The line should continue moving in the distance, making the tension between momentum and intervention clear.

Permitted literal elements:
An industrial production line
Sealed process containers with no labels or logos
Emergency stop cords
Workers examining warning gauges
A bright exit at the far end of the line

Abstraction level:
medium

Story-specific forbidden elements:
Racks
Chips
Laptops
Robots
Clouds
Shields
Arrows
Charts
Skyscrapers
Chess
Handshakes
Split-screen conflict
Rendered text
Logos
Artist imitation

Likely failure modes to avoid:
Do not depict AI as a humanoid machine or literal monster.
Do not imply that a catastrophic event has already occurred.
Do not make the safety intervention look fully successful or fully futile; preserve uncertainty.
Do not add unsupported physical details about specific AI laboratories or facilities.

Global factual restrictions:
Do not fabricate visible factual evidence. Do not imitate a named or living artist. Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
Do not render any words, letters, numbers, labels, captions, annotations, signage, diagrams with text, logos, watermarks, or pseudo-writing anywhere in the image.
If the concept cannot be represented without visible text, represent the relationship through shape, scale, spacing, direction, grouping, interruption, containment, or contrast instead.
